body.statement: Suppose \(0<\eta\leq1/4\).  Fix a nonnegative symmetric \(C^1\) density \(\varphi\) supported on \((-1,1)\) and \(0<\delta<1/8\), and put \(\varphi_\delta(u)=\delta^{-1}\varphi(u/\delta)\), \(b_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta\|_\infty\), \(l_\delta=\|\varphi_\delta'\|_\infty\), \(M_\delta=\max\{b_\delta,b_\delta^2\}\), and \(L_\delta=\max\{l_\delta,2b_\delta l_\delta\}\).  Suppose the declared envelopes satisfy \(M\geq M_\delta\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\).  Applying the same separated bump kernels to the two full laws \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) in \(\mathfrak E_3\) gives two laws in that bounded-Lipschitz envelope class.  They satisfy the maintained event-order and terminal-monotonicity restrictions, have identical smoothed control and treated within-arm laws, and induce the same observable distribution under the common randomized treatment and full-horizon censoring mechanisms.  Their values of \(\ell_\star\) remain \(-1/20\) and \(1/4\).  Hence every causal class with such envelope constants that contains both smoothed laws is non-point-identified for \(\ell_\star\), without any implication that the marked-capacity image is sharp in a larger nonmonotone class.  No conclusion is asserted for fixed envelope constants below \(M_\delta\) or \(L_\delta\).
body.justification: The common-kernel calculation proves observational equivalence inside each envelope class large enough to contain the fixed kernels.
body.gap: Equality of smoothed within-arm laws and kernel-dependent envelope membership both require proof; neither follows from the atomic witness alone.
body.consumer: Users may invoke the smooth nonidentification pair exactly when \(M\geq M_\delta\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\), without inferring enlarged-class sharpness.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the bump system from the repaired strict-support proposition: a nonnegative symmetric \(C^1\) density \(\varphi\), a bandwidth \(0<\delta<1/8\), and the constants \(M_\delta\) and \(L_\delta\) defined there.  Assume \(M\geq M_\delta\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\geq L_\delta\), and use the same kernels under both signs.  Let \(H_{i,\delta}\) be the death bump centered at \(d_i^\star\), let \(J_{j,\delta}\) be the readmission bump centered at \(r_j^\star\), and retain point masses for the \(\infty\) categories.

Under either sign, the smoothed control within-arm law is
\[
\mu_{0,\delta}^{\pm}
=\sum_i\left(\sum_{h,j}q^\pm_{ihj}\right)
(H_{i,\delta}\otimes\delta_\infty)
=\sum_i\frac14(H_{i,\delta}\otimes\delta_\infty),                  \tag{39}
\]
so it is common to the two laws.  For the treated arm, the conditional law of \((D(1),R(1))\) given the categorical pair \((h,j)\) is \(H_{h,\delta}\otimes J_{j,\delta}\), even when the cross-world death draws are shared in an equal-death cell.  Hence
\[
\mu_{1,\delta}^{\pm}
=\sum_{h,j}\left(\sum_iq^\pm_{ihj}\right)
(H_{h,\delta}\otimes J_{j,\delta})
=\sum_{h,j}\mu_{1,hj}^\star
(H_{h,\delta}\otimes J_{j,\delta}),                                \tag{40}
\]
which is also common.  These identities prove equality of the complete smoothed within-arm laws, not only equality of death margins.

The repaired strict-support proposition proves from the separated supports that both laws satisfy \(D(0)\leq D(1)\) and \(R(z)<D(z)\) whenever \(R(z)<\infty\).  It also proves, using the explicit kernel norms, that every finite-part within-arm density is bounded by \(M_\delta\) and is \(L_\delta\)-Lipschitz.  The two assumed inequalities on \(M\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\) therefore put both laws in the declared envelope class.

Use under both signs the same degenerate covariate, independent treatment with probability \(1/2\), and \(C=\tau=3\).  By consistency, for every measurable observed-path set \(A\),
\[
\Pr_{\pm,\delta}(O\in A)
=\frac12\sum_{z=0}^1
\int\mathbf 1\{\mathcal O(z,d,r,3)\in A\}\,
d\mu_{z,\delta}^\star(d,r).                                        \tag{41}
\]
Equations (39)--(40) make the right side independent of the sign, proving observational equivalence.  No bump support crosses a threshold \(1,2,3\), so the survivor denominators and the three numerators defining \(\ell_\star\) are unchanged.  Because \(0<\eta\leq1/4\), those coordinates belong to \(\mathcal H_\eta\), and the two laws retain
\[
\ell_\star=-\frac1{20}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\ell_\star=\frac14.                                                 \tag{42}
\]

Every causal class with the stated envelope regime that contains both laws therefore has, at the common observed distribution (41), an identified set for \(\ell_\star\) containing the two values in (42), separated by \(3/10\).  This proves non-point-identification.  It is a two-witness containment argument only; it neither proves envelope membership below the explicit kernel bounds nor characterizes the capacity image after terminal monotonicity is removed.
